result:
`validateApp` now rejects apps without an owner, and all three apps that call it pass one. Every PR passed CI, merged, and deployed with CD green. I ran `npm run build` on each app and the contract check passed, but I didn't check the deployed apps.

| PR | Repo | Change |
|---|---|---|
| #1 | contracts | `validateApp` throws if `owner` is missing or empty. Released as `@mfe/shared-contracts` 2.0.0 (major, since it breaks existing callers). |
| #2 | shell | Passes `owner: 'platform'` and adopts `^2.0.0`, with an updated lockfile. |
| #3 | billing | Passes `owner: 'payments'` and adopts `^2.0.0`, with an updated lockfile. |
| #4 | reports | Passes `owner: 'insights'` and adopts `^2.0.0`, with an updated lockfile. |

Each owner value comes from the app's `team` field in its `package.json`.

The reports app also calls `validateApp` but had no sub-task. I included it (PR #4) because it would have failed at startup once it picked up 2.0.0. I did not check `libs-platform-kit`, which has no clone listed as a caller.

Nothing slowed me down. The apps pick up the new contract only when they update their dependency, so the library release had to land before the three app PRs.
